about: For whoever translates a page. `keep` is written exactly as is in every language; `rules` apply to every translation. Add to it when a translation gets something wrong.
rules: Never translate people's names, pet names, team names that are names, brands, companies, products, shops, restaurants, venues or street addresses.
Cities and countries take the target language's usual name (Lisbon → Lisboa in Spanish); smaller real places keep their own name.
Keep Kubernetes and command-line output exactly: object kinds, resource names, namespaces, commands, flags, file paths, versions, field names and status values like Ready or CrashLoopBackOff.
Keep music notation exactly: chord symbols (C, Am7, G/B), note names (E3, G4), tempos and time signatures.
Keep numbers, currencies, units, dates, times, emoji and punctuation marks that carry meaning (•, ·, →) as they are, adapting only number words and the order the target language needs.
Keep every {{placeholder}} exactly as written, once each; move it where the target grammar needs it.
Keep Markdown structure (headings, lists, tables, links, code) and translate only the prose.
Write short, plain, friendly interface language a non-technical person understands, matching the length and tone of the source. Use the informal 'you' where the language has one (tú, du, tu).
